Stage prints ceil((x x 1.1)) but evaluates it in floating point: 50*1.1=55.00000000000001, 100*1.1=110.00000000000001, so the stage shows A=56 at Required=50 (exact 55), A=100 at 90 (exact 99), A=111 at 100 (exact 110) and A=122 at 110 (exact 121); the "Full scale" caption shows 133 where the exact maximum is 132. The claim "results are computed by the printed expressions" is false at those slider stops. FIX (builder, resource-specs.json): formulaA -> ["ceil",["/",["*","x",11],10]] (integer arithmetic, exact at every slider stop). Then recheck A at 50/90/100/110 = 55/99/110/121 and full scale 132.

"The formulas match only at that crossover" (one hundred) is false. Exactly, ceil(1.1x)=x+ceil(0.1x), which equals x+10 for every 90<x<=100, so the orders match at 95 and 100 on this slider. With the present float bug the stage instead shows a tie at 90 (A=100,B=100) and none at 100 (A=111,B=110), contradicting the sentence a second way. FIX (principle text; reveal and recall.why copy it): replace the last sentence with "The two orders are equal for requirements from 91 to 100 (95 and 100 on this slider); above 100 the percentage order is larger." Keep "At forty, 10% is four; at one hundred, 10% is ten." (both true). Apply with the c2 formula fix.

The recall answer is right (Required=55: B = 55+10 = 65; options 65/61/67, only 65 is B). But the claim text, and the recall.why shown to the learner, embed the false sentence "The formulas match only at that crossover". FIX: same replacement sentence as c3 in recall.why and in this claim text; then re-verify.
